name: groundtruth
title: GroundTruth (Funnel OS)
description: Reporting and attribution for DriveFunnels clients. Four exports arrive — ads spend, leads, attendance, sales — plus Microsoft Clarity scroll curves, and GT answers what the money did, in many cuts.

integration_key.recommended_for: AcqOS, which calls a fixed set of routes
integration_key.warning: Four of these routes create users, grant client access, replace funnel schemas and write ad spend. Do not give this key to a caller that chooses its own requests at runtime.

hazards.summary: A route that needs a staff session answers 307 to /login. A client that follows redirects receives 200 OK with text/html, not an error.
hazards.detail: Middleware redirects rather than refusing, so res.ok is true and the body is a login page. Sending an integration key does not change this — middleware never consults it for these routes. Any skill marked callable:false will fail this way if attempted.
hazards.mitigation: Never call a skill with callable:false. If you must probe, use redirect:'manual' and treat 307 as a refusal.

hazards.summary: The four refusal codes exist only as string literals in route bodies. No schema, no exported constant.
hazards.detail: A rename in GT would break callers silently. This manifest is currently the only machine-readable copy.

hazards.summary: A single read takes roughly 850ms and five concurrent reads about 3s on the current Supabase instance.
hazards.detail: Instance size, not query cost. Budget timeouts accordingly; do not interpret slowness as failure.

handle_taken.meaning: A DIFFERENT AcqOS client already holds this handle.
handle_taken.action: Mint a different handle and claim again.

source_holds_other.meaning: THIS AcqOS client already holds a different handle.
source_holds_other.action: Stop. Use the handle returned in heldHandle. Do not mint another.

handle_mismatch.meaning: That handle belongs to a different AcqOS client.
handle_mismatch.action: Do not retry. Resolve ownership first.

errors._note: handle_taken and source_holds_other share status 409 and want OPPOSITE actions. Branch on the code field, never on the status.

_unlabelled.503: GT is missing a key or its service-role key. GT's problem, not the caller's. Retrying will not help.
_unlabelled.500: GT fault. Safe to retry once.

skills.name: read-actuals
skills.ask: What are this client's totals for this window, and is the data complete?
skills.returns: Whole-funnel totals, the client's journey stages, import coverage per source, and unmatched-row counts for the window.

errors.when: clientId, from or to missing or malformed, or from > to
offer passed — refused, because these are whole-funnel totals
unknown clientId

caveats: offer is refused rather than ignored; read the preview_purchases and middle_purchases stages instead.

skills.name: read-exposed-cut
skills.ask: Give me this client month by month.

from.description: Give with to, or omit both for all time.

skills.returns: Rows of { cut_key, cut_label, cut_sub, m }. Metrics are nested under m as an opaque object; keys include spend, leads, att, rev, roas, cpa, leadgen and others.

errors.when: cut not in the enum
from given without to, or from > to
offer not in the enum

caveats: This is the same fo_cut the UI reads, with the same filters. A difference between this and a screen is a difference in windows, not in arithmetic.
Only 8 of roughly 14 UI cuts are exposed. Landing page, class variant and the asset drill-downs are not here.
Blank is never zero. A missing metric key means absent, not nought.

skills.name: read-round-insight
skills.ask: What happened in round 0926-01?

roundId.description: Omit for the most recent round. Required when frozen=only or version is set.

skills.returns: A narrative for one round: numbered steps, what changed upstream, findings, a diagnosis, proposed tests, plus versions[] listing every frozen reading of this round.

errors.when: objective not in the enum
frozen=only or version set without an explicit roundId
unknown clientId, or no frozen insight at the requested version

caveats: Omitting roundId means 'the most recent round', which is resolved by a live calculation — that is why frozen=only refuses it.
versions[] comes back on every response, but there is no endpoint that lists frozen periods across rounds.

skills.name: read-month-insight
skills.ask: What happened in September for this client?

month.description: Omit for the most recent month with data.

skills.returns: A narrative for one month, plus per-product and per-channel breakdowns and the rounds and weeks inside it. This is an analysis, not raw cuts.

errors.when: month is not YYYY-MM
channel passed — refused, this endpoint reports every channel side by side
unknown clientId, or the client has no months of data

caveats: channel is REFUSED here but ACCEPTED on round-insight. Read the byChannel block instead.
A month is the rounds NAMED for it, whole. A round crossing a month boundary belongs to one month, not both.

skills.name: read-frozen-version
skills.ask: Give me exactly the v2 reading of that round, not a live one.

version.description: Omit for the current frozen version.

skills.returns: The stored payload exactly as frozen, with the attribution model and rule version that produced it, plus versions[].

errors.when: roundId omitted
no frozen insight at that version

caveats: Fixing a view does not fix a frozen report — that is the point of this skill.
Same path as read-round-insight; separated here because the intent and the failure modes differ.
For months, use /api/integration/month-insight with the same frozen and version params.

skills.name: check-health
skills.ask: Is GroundTruth up, and which commit is live?
skills.returns: { status: 'ok'|'degraded', checks: { supabase, integrationKey, integrationReadonlyKey }, commit, loginRequired, timestamp }

errors.when: status is degraded — Supabase unreachable or a key missing

caveats: Open by design so a monitor that cannot sign in can use it.
A sibling deployment at fo-main.vercel.app answers {status:'ok'} with NO database behind it. Check the commit field to tell them apart.

skills.name: dry-run-pull
skills.ask: Pull this client's Meta spend for last week but don't write it.

since.description: Give with until, or omit both for a default window.

skills.returns: Counts and the rows that would be written. Nothing is stored.

errors.when: since/until malformed or since > until
window longer than 30 days — a pull is not a backfill

caveats: Reaches the Meta Graph API, so it is slower than a database read.

skills.name: commit-pull
skills.ask: Pull this client's Meta spend for last week and save it.
skills.returns: Counts and the import batch id.

errors.when: window longer than 30 days

caveats: Writes ad spend rows. Run dry-run-pull first and read the counts.
The integration route is NOT rate-limited; the staff route is. Do not loop this.

skills.name: freeze-round
skills.ask: Keep this round's reading as it stands today.

roundId.description: Omit for the most recent round.

replace.description: Required to re-freeze a period that already has a current version, else 409.

force.description: Freeze a round that has not finished. Adds a note recording that it was forced.

skills.returns: { version, supersededVersion, isFirst }. The superseded version stays readable.

errors.when: a current version exists and replace was not set
the round has not ended, or has no end date — pass force

caveats: Stamps attribution_model and rule_version, so an old report can still explain itself after the rules change.
Nothing is overwritten; each freeze is a new version.

skills.name: freeze-month
skills.ask: Keep August's reading as it stands today.

month.description: Omit for the most recent month.

errors.when: a current version exists and replace was not set
the month has not closed — pass force

caveats: Same closure rule as freeze-round.

skills.name: claim-handle
skills.ask: Reserve the handle acme_fitness for this AcqOS client.

clientId.description: The handle GT will know this client by permanently. It becomes client_id on every row.

sourceClientId.description: The AcqOS clients.id. Required — a claim without it is a handle held by nobody.

skills.returns: 201 { claimed: true, adopted } on a fresh claim. 200 { claimed: false, alreadyYours: true } on a retry.

errors.when: clientId fails the slug pattern, or sourceClientId is not a uuid

caveats: Idempotent for the same (handle, sourceClientId) pair — a retry is a 200, not an error.
adopted:true means a handle created by hand was adopted rather than duplicated.
Claiming does NOT make the client visible. Push a funnel schema first.
The handle is permanent. Mint it from something stable, not a display name.

skills.name: push-schema
skills.ask: Replace this client's funnel stages with this list.

stages.description: UNVERIFIED SHAPE — the validator in lib/integration/schema.ts was not read in full. A 400 returns errors[] naming the stage and field, which is the reliable way to learn the shape.

generatedAt.description: Used to refuse a stale push.

createClient.description: Required when the handle has no funnel yet.

skills.returns: { ok, created, stagesWritten, pricesPreserved[], dimensionsPreserved[], rateLabelsPreserved[] }

errors.when: validation failed — errors[] names each bad stage and field
a stage names a dimension or metric GT does not know
unknown clientId and createClient was not true
a newer funnel is already stored — compares generatedAt. Nothing was written.

caveats: WHOLESALE REPLACE. client_journey_config is deleted and rewritten for this client.
THREE FIELDS SURVIVE, keyed by stage_slug: unit_price, compare_dimension, stage_rate_label. Renaming a slug silently drops that stage's price and comparison dimension.
The response names what was preserved. Read it — the stored funnel is not exactly what you sent.

skills.name: grant-login
skills.ask: Give jane@acme.com access to acme_fitness and return me the sign-in link.

sourceClientId.description: Checked against the handle's owner when given.

skills.returns: 201 created:true, or 200 created:false on a retry. Both carry signInLink and note.
caveats: Creates the account with NO password. GT sends no mail — the link is returned for the caller's own welcome email.
signInLink may be null with linkError set. The grant is still written and correct. Retry the LINK, not the onboarding.
Safe to call twice — magiclink, not invite, so a retry still returns a usable link.

skills.name: revoke-login
skills.ask: Take away jane@acme.com's access to acme_fitness.
skills.returns: { ok, revoked }. revoked:false with a reason when there was nothing to revoke — that is a success, not an error.
caveats: The auth user SURVIVES on purpose. AcqOS owns whether the person exists; GT owns what they may read.
The person then sees a 'no client yet' screen rather than a broken login.

skills.name: accept-best-guess

skills.name: assign-identity
skills.ask: This parked row is jane@x.com — assign it.

skills.ask: Close this parked row without counting it.

skills.name: detach

skills.name: list-rules
skills.ask: What rules decide this client's sources?

skills.name: propose-rules-from-data
skills.ask: What sources exist in this client's data that no rule names?

skills.name: create-rule
skills.ask: Add an Affiliate source matching source column = affiliate_partner.

skills.name: delete-rule
skills.ask: Delete the Affiliate source rule.

skills.name: refresh-cache
skills.ask: Drop the cache, I just changed something in the database.

skills.name: read-landing-page-cut
skills.ask: Compare this client's landing pages.
skills.reads: v_metrics_by_lp via fo_cut, rendered in a server component

skills.name: read-class-variant-cut
skills.ask: Compare this client's class variants.

skills.name: drill-into-asset

skills.name: read-answer-split
skills.ask: What did this client's leads say their profession was?

blocked_reasons.staff_session: The route exists but middleware requires a Supabase staff session. There is no key-based door. A call returns 307 to /login, and 200 text/html if redirects are followed.
blocked_reasons.no_route: The capability exists only in the UI, rendered from fo_cut inside a server component. No HTTP endpoint exposes it.
